label: Scenario A
title: Community Health Campaign Dilemma
provenance: Constructed CAPS-aligned classroom stimulus for educator review
content: In a rural community in KwaZulu-Natal, a group of Grade 12 learners from Siyabonga Secondary School launched a health awareness campaign to address rising rates of teenage pregnancy and HIV/AIDS. The campaign, titled 'Know Your Status, Protect Your Future', included peer education workshops, distribution of informational pamphlets, and partnerships with the local clinic. However, after three months, the school governing body raised concerns that some parents felt the campaign promoted sexual activity among minors, despite the learners' emphasis on abstinence and safe sex education. The learners now face a decision: continue the campaign as is, modify it to focus solely on abstinence, or discontinue it due to community pushback.
context: This scenario reflects real-world tensions in Life Orientation education between promoting comprehensive sexual health education and navigating cultural or religious community values, particularly in rural South African contexts. It aligns with CAPS Grade 12 Term 2 focus on 'Social and environmental responsibility' and 'Democracy and human rights'.
usable_evidence: Campaign name: 'Know Your Status, Protect Your Future'
Target issues: Teenage pregnancy and HIV/AIDS
Activities: Peer education workshops, pamphlet distribution, local clinic partnership
Concern raised by: School governing body
Parent concern: Perception that campaign promotes sexual activity among minors
Learners' stated emphasis: Abstinence and safe sex education
Decision options: Continue as is, modify to abstinence-only, or discontinue

label: Decision Tool B
title: Ethical Decision-Making Framework for Health Campaigns
provenance: Constructed CAPS-aligned classroom stimulus for educator review
content: When facing community opposition to health initiatives, learners should use this structured approach: (1) Identify the core values at stake (e.g., health, autonomy, cultural respect); (2) Gather accurate data from trusted sources (e.g., clinic statistics, national health policies); (3) Consult stakeholders respectfully (learners, parents, teachers, health workers); (4) Evaluate options against constitutional rights (Section 27: access to healthcare; Section 10: human dignity); (5) Choose an action that promotes health equity while minimizing harm; (6) Reflect on outcomes and be prepared to adapt. This tool is adapted from the Life Orientation CAPS emphasis on applying democratic values and human rights to real-life contexts.
context: This decision tool supports learners in applying constitutional values and ethical reasoning to community health dilemmas, directly supporting CAPS Grade 12 topics on 'Citizenship education', 'Human rights', and 'Social responsibility'. It provides a scaffold for analysing Scenario A.
usable_evidence: Step 1: Identify core values at stake (health, autonomy, cultural respect)
Step 2: Gather accurate data from trusted sources (clinic stats, national health policies)
Step 3: Consult stakeholders respectfully (learners, parents, teachers, health workers)
Step 4: Evaluate options against constitutional rights (Section 27: healthcare; Section 10: dignity)
Step 5: Choose action promoting health equity while minimizing harm
Step 6: Reflect on outcomes and adapt
Source: Adapted from Life Orientation CAPS application of democratic values and human rights
